coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia 2009 team-season page (infobox + "Personnel > Coaching staff" table, 11 names). (2) Wayback capture of rolltide.com's official football "Coaches" listing from Jan 4, 2010 — three days before the BCS title game — which is the single best contemporaneous source and yields clean "Name - Title" text for 12 people. (3) The 2009 Alabama Football Media Guide PDF (archived on Wayback), pp. 99-104, which is the ONLY enumeration of the broader support staff. (4) Wayback captures of rolltide.com's Sports Medicine staff page from Aug 15, 2009 (preseason) and Feb 12, 2010 (post-championship) — identical rosters, confirming those people were on staff all season.

WHAT IS COMPLETE. The on-field tier is fully recovered: head coach + 9 on-field assistants (Burns, Cignetti, Bo Davis, McElwain, Pendry, Smart, Sunseri, Bobby Williams, Willis), confirmed by three independent sources that agree exactly. Strength & conditioning, graduate assistants, operations/personnel, equipment, and medical tiers are recovered from media guide p. 104 ("FOOTBALL SUPPORT", a 30-person photo grid) plus the dedicated bio pages on pp. 99-103. 48 people total.

MAJOR CAVEAT ON QUOTES FOR 30 OF THE 48. Media guide p. 104 carries no extractable text — verified with two independent PDF text extractors (pypdf and PyMuPDF), both of which return only "FOOTBALL SUPPORT" and the page number. The name/title nameplates are baked into a low-resolution raster (the underlying bitmap is roughly 95x136 px per card), so the title line is about 5 px tall at source resolution. I rendered the page at 600 dpi with PyMuPDF and recovered the titles by autocontrast + 4x Lanczos upscaling. The NAMES are unambiguous and I am confident in all 30 spellings; five of them (Rodney Brown, Ginger Gilmore, Jeremy Gsell, Bill McDonald, Jeff Purinton) independently cross-check against HTML sources with the same titles, which validates the reading method. But the titles are a best-effort image transcription, NOT text that can be copied faithfully, so per instructions those rows carry quote:"" with an explanatory note. Treat the p.104-only titles as high-confidence-but-not-verbatim.

TWO TITLES I COULD NOT READ. Gary Cramer's title renders as "DIRECTOR OF" plus a short illegible token (possibly a 3-letter acronym), and Troy Finney's second title line is illegible ("SENIOR DIRECTOR" is legible; the qualifier is not — context suggests video operations, since the two video graduate assistants report into that area, but I did not read it and am not asserting it). Both are marked in their notes.

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER. (a) ANALYST and QUALITY CONTROL: no person on the 2009 staff carries an "analyst" or "quality control" title in any source I found. This appears to be genuinely accurate for the era rather than a gap — Alabama's off-field coaching support in 2009 was titled as graduate assistants (Agee, Groh, Judge, Norrid, O'Brien, Pope), and the large analyst staffs came later. I found no evidence of an analyst tier to miss. (b) Student managers, student trainers, and video/equipment student staff beyond the one pictured student assistant (Sedrick Irvin) are not enumerated anywhere I could find. (c) Team physicians are named in prose on the Sports Medicine page (Robinson, Buettner, Laubenthal, Fowler, Andrews, Cain) but as department-wide/volunteer/consulting physicians, not football staff, so I excluded them rather than pad the list. (d) The seven department-wide athletic trainers assigned to other sports were excluded for the same reason; only the five sports-medicine people documented as football (Allen, McDonald, Brown, Gilmore, Gsell — all five also pictured on football support p. 104) plus the two football athletic-training graduate assistants (Jacobi, Williams) are included.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS. Kevin Steele (defensive coordinator) and Lance Thompson (linebackers) both left in January 2009, BEFORE the season, and are excluded — Wikipedia documents their departures and the Sunseri/Willis hires that replaced them. No one on this list is documented as arriving or departing mid-season, so no midseason_note fields are set; all 48 are documented as on staff through the championship game.

TOOL LIMITATION. This session's WebSearch quota was exhausted on the first call, so I could not run a contemporary news sweep for additional hire announcements or for corroboration of the harder-to-read titles. Everything here comes from direct URL fetches of primary/archival sources. A news sweep is the obvious next step for anyone wanting to confirm Cramer's and Finney's titles.
